questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: Ram writes a letter.

options.option_text: A letter is wrote by Ram
A letter is written by Ram
A letter was written by Ram
A letter has written by Ram

questions.explanation: Simple present active → 'is/are + V3' passive. Object 'a letter' → subject; subject 'Ram' → 'by Ram'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: They are painting the wall.

options.option_text: The wall is painted by them
The wall is being painted by them
The wall was being painted by them
The wall has been painted by them

questions.explanation: Present continuous active ('are painting') → 'is/are being + V3' passive.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: She has finished the report.

options.option_text: The report is finished by her
The report has been finished by her
The report was finished by her
The report had been finished by her

questions.explanation: Present perfect active ('has finished') → 'has/have been + V3' passive.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: Open the door.

options.option_text: The door is opened
Let the door be opened
The door was opened
The door has been opened

questions.explanation: Imperative → 'Let + object + be + V3' passive. Covers commands like 'shut the gate' → 'Let the gate be shut'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: Who taught you French?

options.option_text: By whom were you taught French?
By who was French taught you?
Whom taught French to you?
Who was French taught by?

questions.explanation: Who → By whom (preposition + object form). Auxiliary before subject for interrogative: 'were you taught…'. Main verb 'teach' → 'taught' (V3).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: They will announce the results tomorrow.

options.option_text: The results will announced tomorrow
The results will be announced tomorrow
The results are announced tomorrow
The results would be announced tomorrow

questions.explanation: Simple future active → 'will/shall be + V3' passive. Agent 'they' can be dropped when unimportant.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: The boy must finish the task.

options.option_text: The task must finished by the boy
The task must be finished by the boy
The task has been finished by the boy
The task was finished by the boy

questions.explanation: Modal + bare infinitive active ('must finish') → 'modal + be + V3' passive. Same for can/could/should/may/might/ought to.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive: She gave him a book.

options.option_text: He was given a book by her
He had been given a book by her
He has given a book by her
He was gave a book by her

questions.explanation: Two objects (he + book). Either can become the subject of the passive. The indirect-object option 'He was given a book by her' is usually preferred in exam keys. 'A book was given to him by her' is also valid but usually not the keyed form.
questions.subject: English
